title: A result that doesn't match: reproducing someone's image

questions.q: Which of these removes the graph from a PNG?
questions.why: The graph is in text chunks of that one file. A screenshot is a new image.

questions.q: You want the third image of a batch of 4, on a 512 by 512 SD latent. Which gives the same noise?
options: LatentFromBatch with index 2 from the same batch settings
Any seed with the same prompt
questions.answer: LatentFromBatch with index 2 from the same batch settings
questions.why: All noise comes from one generator, and batch_index picks the item. This works because each item holds a multiple of 16 values (CU-240). The lab checks each option.

questions.q: Does a different graphics card change the noise from a seed in core KSampler?
options: No, it is drawn on the CPU
Yes, each card has its own
questions.answer: No, it is drawn on the CPU
questions.why: prepare_noise_inner uses device='cpu'. What follows runs on the card and can differ.

questions.q: In our one-seed test, how did euler and ddim compare on SD 1.5?
questions.why: renders.json holds the same SHA-256 for both.

questions.q: What does the file name in a graph prove?
options: Only what the file was called
questions.answer: Only what the file was called
questions.why: Names are not identities. Compare hashes.

options: Slower deterministic algorithms where possible, and not in all cases
The same noise on every card
questions.answer: Slower deterministic algorithms where possible, and not in all cases
questions.why: Its help says this might not make images deterministic in all cases.
